full_judgment: 6. Learned Advocate Mr Mamun Chowdhury has appeared on behalf of the opposite party No. 9. His contention is that, admittedly the defendant Nos. 1-8 and the plaintiff are all heirs of deceased Haji Rabban Uddin. He also points out that, the defendant No. 11, Most Halema Akhter is in fact wife of late Haji Rabban Uddin, who died leaving 2 (two) wives, one of whom is the plaintiff and another is defendant No. 11 could and, as such, the plaintiff and the defendant No. 11 could jointly claim to the extent of the share in the properties left by the deceased Haji Rabban Uddin, as described in the 1st schedule to the plaint. The learned Advocate next submits that, there are as many as 124 serial numbers of properties in the 1st schedule to the plaint, which refers to the 16 annas properties of the deceased Haji Rabban Uddin and out of this 16 annas property, the learned Advocate procee6 on, only the property described in RS plot No. 2091 and 2092, as described against serial Nos. 33 and 34, have been sold to the plaintiff, by 3 (three) registered sale deeds as mentioned in the 2nd schedule to the plaint, and it has also been admitted by the plaintiff that, the executants of the said 3 sale deeds are defendant Nos. 1-8, who are respectively the sons and daughters of the deceased Haji Rabban Uddin and, apparently, the plaintiff did not pray for any injunction against these defendants Nos. 1-8. On the other hand, the suit property sold by the defendant Nos. 1-8 to respondent-opposite party No. 9 are only a portion of 16 annas property of the said deceased Haji Rabban Uddin, while there are other properties in the same mouza as described in 1st schedule to the plaint. He next argues that, the title and possession of the defendant No. 1-8 in the RS plot Nos. 2091 and 2092 have not been disputed and they have sold the same for consideration and by giving specific boundary to the sale deeds and have also handed over the possession of the same to the defendant No. 9 and the defendant No. 9 has been possessing and enjoying the same, since the date of transfer. He also submits that, the respondent-opposite party No. 9 has purchased the suit property of RS Plot No. 2091 and 2092 after final publication of khatian (Annexure-1 series) and thereafter found good title and possession of the sellers in property sold to it. He, therefore, maintains that, in passing the impugned judgment and order, the trial court has committed no error of law and, as such, this Rule has no merit and the same may be discharged and, in consequence, the FMA No. 225 of 2019 has also no merit and may be dismissed.
